chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhassan ibn Ahmad from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sent his hunting dog, and the dog caught the prey and it had been killed (by the dog). He said: 'Eat it, even if the dog ate from it.'

key_terms.كَلْبُ: Dog (specifically hunting dog in this context)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat meat if the hunting dog eats part of it before being retrieved?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the permissibility of the prey depends on the dog being trained and sent in God's name, rather than the condition of the meat at retrieval. The ruling that the meat remains halal even if the dog eats from it highlights the Shia juristic view that the act of hunting itself sanctifies the catch, distinguishing it from general consumption. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the validity of meat from wild animals hunted by dogs.
